column1: **Fix hygiene first.** Cleanliness/hygiene is the most frequent complaint (1,497 negative reviews, 30.7%). Introduce daily room/bathroom inspection checklists and follow up on any review that mentions dirt, smell or pests.

**Run preventive maintenance on bathrooms, bedding and AC.** Bathroom reviews are 52.0% negative; Bed / bedding reviews are 55.7% negative; Air conditioning reviews are 50.8% negative versus 18.6% overall - these are fixable equipment/linen issues.

**Invest in staff conduct and responsiveness.** Rude/unhelpful staff appears in 992 negative reviews and slow/poor service in 570. Add service-recovery training and a response-time target for complaints.

**Prioritise and quality-check amenities.** Spa and similar amenities are associated with a higher rating-positive share (+13.2 pp); amenities such as Air conditioning are often mentioned in complaints (net +0.0 pp), so guarantee they work reliably rather than just listing them.

**Use review sentiment as an early-warning indicator.** VADER's compound score separates 1-2 star from 4-5 star reviews well (ROC-AUC 0.95); alert managers when a hotel's share of negative reviews rises, and monitor the top pain-point counts monthly.

**Combine text sentiment with the hotel-success model.** Hotel-level mean sentiment is positively related to the hotel's rating (Spearman 0.64). Because success was defined from rating, use sentiment and pain points as *diagnostic* features beside Review 1's predictors, validated on a proper train/test split, rather than as extra predictors of the same label.
**Benchmark within hotel category.** Negative-text share ranges from 7.6% (5-star hotel) to 24.0% (2-star hotel); compare a hotel with peers of the same category rather than the overall average.

**Collect richer feedback.** 25.2% of reviews are 5 words or fewer and neutral (3-star) reviews are hardest to interpret (VADER F1 0.14); use short guided prompts (e.g. room, staff, value) to capture usable detail.
